answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging every identity a refundable timber bond: each agent locks collateral that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate accounts. Influence then flows through a verification vertex where attestations from established agents are weighted by their own staked history, so a swarm of fresh clones starts with near-zero weight. A forger launching a thousand comet-fast sockpuppets must fund a thousand bonds and wait out the same slow trust-building as everyone else, turning cheap identity spam into an expensive, slow, and detected investment.
